items.informal_name: Infinite Rational Approximations to Irrational Numbers with Denominator Squared Bound
items.informal_description: For any irrational real number $\xi$, the set of rational numbers $q$ (in lowest terms) satisfying $|\xi - q| < 1 / (\text{den}(q))^2$ is infinite, where $\text{den}(q)$ denotes the denominator of $q$.
A real number $ x $ is called a Liouville number if, for every natural number $ n $, there exist integers $ a $ and $ b $ with $ b > 1 $ such that $ 0 < |x - \frac{a}{b}| < \frac{1}{b^n} $.

items.informal_name: Infinite Rational Approximations with $ |\xi - q| < 1/\text{den}(q)^2 $ iff Irrational
items.informal_description: A real number $\xi$ is irrational if and only if there are infinitely many rational numbers $q$ such that the absolute difference $|\xi - q|$ is strictly less than $1 / \text{den}(q)^2$, where $\text{den}(q)$ denotes the denominator of $q$ when expressed in lowest terms.

items.informal_name: Frequent Rational Approximation of Liouville Numbers
items.type: ∀ {x : ℝ}, Liouville x → ∀ (n : ℕ), ∃ᶠ (b : ℕ) in Filter.atTop, ∃ a, x ≠ ↑a / ↑b ∧ |x - ↑a / ↑b| < 1 / ↑b ^ n
items.informal_description:
For any Liouville number $x$ and every natural number $n$, there exist infinitely many natural numbers $b$ and integers $a$ such that $x 
eq  rac{a}{b}$ and $\left|x -  rac{a}{b}\right| <  rac{1}{b^n}$.

A real number $ x $ is called a Liouville number with exponent $ p $ if there exists a positive constant $ C $ such that for infinitely many natural numbers $ n $, there exists an integer $ m $ where $ x 
eq  rac{m}{n} $ and the absolute difference $ |x -  rac{m}{n}| $ is less than $  rac{C}{n^p} $.

items.informal_name: Liouville's Approximation Theorem for Irrational Roots of Integer Polynomials
items.type:
∀ {α : ℝ},
  Irrational α →
    ∀ {f : Polynomial ℤ},
      f ≠ 0 →
        Polynomial.eval α (Polynomial.map (algebraMap ℤ ℝ) f) = 0 →
          ∃ A, 0 < A ∧ ∀ (a : ℤ) (b : ℕ), 1 ≤ (↑b + 1) ^ f.natDegree * (|α - ↑a / (↑b + 1)| * A)
items.informal_description: Let $\alpha$ be an irrational real number and let $f \in \mathbb{Z}[X]$ be a non-zero polynomial such that $f(\alpha) = 0$. Then there exists a positive real number $A$ such that for all integers $a$ and natural numbers $b$, the inequality $1 \leq A \cdot (b + 1)^{\deg(f)} \cdot |\alpha - \frac{a}{b + 1}|$ holds.

A real number $ x $ satisfies the Liouville condition with exponent $ 1 $, meaning there exists a positive constant $ C $ such that for infinitely many natural numbers $ n $, there exists an integer $ m $ with $ x \neq \frac{m}{n} $ and $ \left|x - \frac{m}{n}\right| < \frac{C}{n} $.

items.informal_name: The Liouville Number Generated by $ m $ is a Liouville Number
items.informal_description: For any natural number $ m \geq 2 $, the Liouville number constructed as the infinite sum $ \sum_{i=0}^{\infty} \frac{1}{m^{i!}} $ satisfies the definition of a Liouville number: for every natural number $ n $, there exist integers $ a $ and $ b > 1 $ such that $ 0 < \left|x - \frac{a}{b}\right| < \frac{1}{b^n} $.

items.informal_name: Frequent Rational Approximations for Liouville Numbers with Exponent $ p $
items.type: ∀ {p q x : ℝ}, LiouvilleWith p x → q < p → ∃ᶠ (n : ℕ) in Filter.atTop, ∃ m, x ≠ ↑m / ↑n ∧ |x - ↑m / ↑n| < ↑n ^ (-q)
items.informal_description:
For a real number $ x $ that is a Liouville number with exponent $ p $, and for any real number $ q < p $, there exist infinitely many natural numbers $ n $ and integers $ m $ such that $ x 
eq  rac{m}{n} $ and the absolute difference $ |x -  rac{m}{n}| $ is less than $ n^{-q} $. This holds frequently in the sense of the filter at top, meaning for infinitely many $ n $.

items.informal_name: Existence of Positive Constants for Liouville Numbers with Exponent p
items.type:
∀ {p x : ℝ},
  LiouvilleWith p x →
    ∃ C, ∃ (_ : 0 < C), ∃ᶠ (n : ℕ) in Filter.atTop, 1 ≤ n ∧ ∃ m, x ≠ ↑m / ↑n ∧ |x - ↑m / ↑n| < C / ↑n ^ p
items.informal_description: For a real number $x$ that is a Liouville number with exponent $p$, there exists a positive real constant $C$ such that for infinitely many natural numbers $n$, there exists an integer $m$ where $x \neq \frac{m}{n}$ and the absolute difference $\left|x - \frac{m}{n}\right|$ is less than $\frac{C}{n^p}$.

items.informal_name: Existence of Improved Rational Approximations for Irrational Numbers with Quadratic Denominator Bound
items.informal_description: For any irrational real number $\xi$ and any rational number $q$, there exists a rational number $q'$ such that $|\xi - q'| < 1/(\text{den}(q'))^2$ and $|\xi - q'| < |\xi - q|$, where $\text{den}(q')$ denotes the denominator of $q'$ in lowest terms.

items.informal_name: Lower Bound on Distance from Irrational to Rationals with Bounded Denominators
items.type: ∀ {x : ℝ}, Irrational x → ∀ (n : ℕ), ∀ᶠ (ε : ℝ) in nhds 0, ∀ k ≤ n, ∀ (m : ℤ), ε ≤ dist x (↑m / ↑k)
items.informal_description: For any irrational number $x$ and natural number $n$, there exists a neighborhood around zero such that for all sufficiently small $\varepsilon$ in this neighborhood, every rational number $\frac{m}{k}$ with $k \leq n$ satisfies $|x - \frac{m}{k}| \geq \varepsilon$.
